gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states the full cost of Apple's own strap setup: case plus Crossbody Strap comes to $49 + $59 = $108 with the Silicone Case or $59 + $59 = $118 with the TechWoven Case, versus one Bandolier set price. Nor does it give the strap's 42.5–81.9 in (1.08–2.08 m) adjustment range.
standout_why: Macworld (opened) mentions only lanyard-slot cases (Beats, Spigen Classic LS), with no prices, no strap length and no combined cost. I could not open AppleInsider (403), WIRED, Travel + Leisure (fetch blocked) or Bandolier's own pages (429). AppleInsider's article is titled 'Apple's iPhone 17 crossbody strap is too expensive', so it very likely already states the $59 strap price and may compare the total. That makes this at most partly new.
decides: It frames the pick as a total-cost question. Apple's strap only works with Apple's TechWoven or Silicone cases (it attaches to them, not to the phone), so the real Apple price is $108–$118 for a case plus one crossbody strap with no wristlet. ChatGPT quoted Bandolier's Palmer Duet at $98 with a crossbody chain and a wristlet, but I could not verify that price. If it holds, the Bandolier set costs less than Apple's for more pieces. The $27–$32 rope-strap cases ChatGPT showed are the budget tier. Apple's 1.08–2.08 m continuous adjustment is the one sourced length spec, so it is the figure to quote for tall wearers or for wearing the phone short at the hip.
